glosses: (honorific) be in a state of having …
patterns.usage_note: Honorific counterpart of 〜ている, used of the listener or a third party you are elevating; for your own side you switch to 〜ております, and the plain form is 〜ている. 〜ておいでになる is a near-equivalent that is often felt to be a shade more formal. Note that でいらっしゃる also attaches to nouns and adjectives (お元気でいらっしゃる, 部長でいらっしゃる), an attachment outside the verbal te-form pattern shown here.

examples.ruby: 先生[せんせい]は今[いま]、論文[ろんぶん]を書[か]いていらっしゃいます。
examples.english: The professor is working on a paper at the moment.

examples.ruby: 奥様[おくさま]は庭[にわ]の花[はな]に水[みず]をあげていらっしゃる。
examples.english: Your wife is out watering the flowers in the garden.

examples.ruby: 会長[かいちょう]は毎年[まいとし]この式典[しきてん]に出席[しゅっせき]していらっしゃる。
examples.english: The chairman attends this ceremony every year.

glosses: be in the state of having …
patterns.usage_note: The neutral, default progressive/resultative: with an activity verb it marks an action in progress, with a change-of-state verb the state that resulted. 〜てる and 〜でる are the everyday contracted forms in speech; 〜ていらっしゃる is the honorific and 〜ております the humble counterpart. Politeness is carried by the ます ending, not by the pattern itself.

examples.ruby: 妹[いもうと]は好[す]きな音楽[おんがく]をずっと聴[き]いている。
examples.english: My little sister has been listening to her favorite music this whole time.

examples.ruby: 猫[ねこ]はまだソファの上[うえ]に寝[ね]そべっています。
examples.english: The cat is still stretched out on the sofa.

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]はさっきから宿題[しゅくだい]の続[つづ]きをしてる。
examples.english: My little brother's been plugging away at the rest of his homework.

patterns.usage_note: Two quite different lives: 〜ております is the humble-polite 〜ている used about yourself, your family or your company in business and public speech, while plain 〜ておる about someone else is not honorific at all; in standard Japanese it sounds blunt, condescending or archaic, so use 〜ている or 〜ていらっしゃる instead. The contracted 〜とる／〜どる is a Western-Japan colloquial equivalent of 〜てる and carries no humility at all.

examples.ruby: ただ今[いま]、担当[たんとう]の者[もの]が席[せき]を外[はず]しております。
examples.english: I'm afraid the person handling this is away from their desk right now.

examples.ruby: 父[ちち]は昼[ひる]から縁側[えんがわ]でビールを飲[の]んどる。
examples.english: Dad's been out on the veranda drinking beer since noon.

examples.ruby: 弊社[へいしゃ]では新[あら]たな支援[しえん]制度[せいど]を設[もう]けております。
examples.english: We have a new support program in place here at our company.
